text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
QADISSIYA
- Arab and foreign parties urge world public opinion to pressure Iran to release Iraqi POWs.
- Pakistani president receives head of Iraqi delegation to an Islamic meeting in Islamabad.
- Egyptian students demonstrate against Israel.
- Sudanese army achieves victories over rebels.
- More violence reported in occupied territories in Palestine.
- Arab observers to monitor elections in Algeria.
- Trade ministry lowers price of essential goods ferried to state-owned supermarkets.
- Iraq and Egypt discuss parliamentary relations.
- Iraq and Jordan cooperate in energy fields.
- French official harshly criticises U.S. policy toward Iraq.
(The above were also carried by AL-IRAQ and JUMHOURIYA)
- Article suggests ways to reform Iraq's banking system.
- French companies prepared to supply Iraq with medical goods.
- Article on U.S. aggression on Iraq.
- Three thieves get life sentences for stealing gold.
JUMHOURIYA
- National Assembly reviews Iraq's financial policy.
AL-IRAQ
- Iraqi Kurdistan has turned into a fertile ground for both Iranian and Turkish intelligence officers.
- Article on U.S. lies in foreign policy.
